# What a real Flexo MMS stack does with this project's RDF, measured by
# TestFlexoInterop. This is a ratchet: every line is adjudicated, and a change to
# one is a change in interoperability, not a change in the harness.
#
# Regenerate against a running stack (see .agents/skills/flexo-interop):
#   FLEXO_INTEROP=1 FLEXO_INTEROP_TOKEN=<jwt> \
#     go test -count=1 ./internal/translate/interop/flexo -run TestFlexoInterop -update-flexo
#
# graph-load is the Turtle this project writes, loaded through Layer 1's graph
# endpoint. json-commit is the same model posted through the SysML v2 service's
# own commit path: the ground truth for what its read path can carry at all.
# Server-generated commit ids, timestamps and durations are not recorded.

[findings]
graph-load: 49 of 49 elements listed, 369 of 452 properties delivered
json-commit: 33 of 33 elements listed, 158 of 158 properties delivered
graph-load: 10 properties are in the sysx: extension namespace and are dropped unread — extractModelElementToJson ignores every predicate outside the sysml: vocabulary and the JSON annotation namespace (sysx:argumentIndex, sysx:declaredKeyword, sysx:endForm, sysx:endIndex, sysx:hasBody, sysx:memberIndex, sysx:relatedFeature, sysx:sourceLanguage, sysx:sourceTail, sysx:sourceText)
graph-load: 14 of 15 multi-valued properties are delivered (sysml:ownedFeature on 2/2, sysml:ownedFeatureMembership on 2/2, sysml:ownedMember on 3/3, sysml:ownedMembership on 3/3, sysml:ownedRelationship on 3/3, sysml:specializes on 1/1, sysx:relatedFeature on 0/1); a standard predicate with several values is skipped entirely unless a JSON annotation supplies the array
graph-load: the roots endpoint reports 9 of 49 elements as roots (9 have no owner in the model); it filters on sysml:owner and sysml:owningRelatedElement
json-commit: the roots endpoint reports 1 of 33 elements as roots, 1 in the payload
both: the element listing answered every element it has in 1 response(s) at pageSize=10 — the service accepts pageAfter/pageBefore/pageSize and ignores them
json-commit: 6 of 6 multi-valued properties are delivered (aliasIds on 1/1, connectorEnd on 1/1, ownedElement on 3/3, ownedSpecialization on 1/1), because the commit path stores each array whole as a JSON annotation literal alongside the typed triples
graph-load: 0 of 49 subjects of the graph are expression nodes or other subjects outside the element namespace
